title: Running a similarity search and tuning top-k

videos.script: Ask the help centre whether Marginalia sells concert tickets. It does not. The search answers anyway, with three articles. {{tickets}} That is not a bug. A top-k search returns the k nearest articles, whatever they are. It never says it found nothing. {{nearest}} This lesson is about the two dials that decide what comes back. The first is k itself. {{k}} You will measure how many questions find their answer as k grows from one to ten, and what each extra article costs downstream. {{curve}} The second is a score below which you return nothing. You will see where that line sits for one model, and why it moves for another. {{threshold}} Then the index gets a say. Ask PostgreSQL for a hundred rows through an HNSW index, and it hands back forty. No error, no warning. {{forty}} Last, a pattern that buys precision cheaply. Fetch a wide set with a fast pass, then score just those again with something better. {{rerank}} By the end you can choose k on purpose, and know when the database chose it for you. {{end}}
